tests/fixtures/stripboard/negative/ - the grader's negative fixtures
====================================================================

One fixture per hard constraint, TWO for HC10, and a `healthy` board on which
all ten hold. Every one of them is named for the constraint it must make fail,
and tests/stripboard/grade.test.ts asserts that THAT constraint failed and that
its detail names the offending thing - not merely that something failed.

A fixture is up to five files. Each falls back to `healthy`'s when absent, so a
fixture declares only what it changes:

  <name>.dump              the board, as --dump-board prints one
  <name>.footprints.json   designator -> the KiCad footprint it is fitted with
  <name>.netlist           the reference export, read by referenceNetsFromExport
  <name>.report            --check's output, verbatim
  <name>.status            --check's exit code, beside the report

WHY DUMP TEXT AND NOT BOARDS
----------------------------
The grader's real input seam is text: it reads a dump, a --check report and a
netlist export. So the fixtures are those three things, and no test in
grade.test.ts spawns a binary. The two fixtures that ARE captures are captures
because the state they carry cannot be hand-written honestly - see below.

THE FIXTURES, AND WHERE EACH CAME FROM
--------------------------------------

healthy                     HAND-WRITTEN. Three parts - two DIN0207 resistors
                            and a 1x02 header - on a 10 x 40 canvas, with one
                            wire. All ten hold on it. Every hand-written
                            negative below is this board with ONE thing wrong,
                            so a fixture isolates its constraint rather than
                            failing for several reasons at once.

incomplete-net              HAND-WRITTEN REPORT, over the healthy board. HC1
                            reads --check's output, so the fixture IS that
                            output: `bottom incomplete` under Layout state,
                            exit 1.

cuts-unresolved             CAPTURED, and it has to be. --dump-board on
                            boards/transistor-preamp-lab/transistor-preamp-lab.perfboard.vrt
                            with the binary veroroute.pin names. It reports
                            CUT_STATE UNRESOLVED with 19 CUT_CONFLICT lines,
                            GRID 29 46 and BOUNDS 6,4 28,40. Its .report is
                            that board's REAL --check output (exit 1), not a
                            hand-written one, and its .footprints.json is
                            derived from the board's own committed export
                            tests/fixtures/transistor-preamp-lab.net - all 31
                            placed parts resolve, which was measured rather
                            than assumed.
                            It is also the board whose J = -1 Task 11 refuses,
                            from the other direction.

floated-part                HAND-WRITTEN, and the deviation from the task
                            brief's fixture list is deliberate and recorded
                            here. The brief names the committed
                            tests/fixtures/pultec-low-boost-c19-floated.dump.
                            That capture CANNOT go through the full table: it
                            places `board_terminals` (BLOCK_200MIL3, three
                            pins), whose footprint is recorded nowhere in this
                            repository, so PAR2 refuses the whole grade before
                            HC3 reports anything - and PAR2 refusing it is
                            CORRECT. So the V4 fixture is the healthy board
                            with one part floated, named C19 to mirror the
                            measured failure, and the real capture is graded by
                            hc3 DIRECTLY in grade.test.ts, which needs no
                            footprint map at all. The measured failure is still
                            used, and used by the real check.

span-above-tool-range       NOT FILES. These three are CONSTRUCTED in
span-above-reach            tests/stripboard/grade-fixtures.ts (SPAN_FIXTURES),
span-below-minimum          which names a footprint, reads that family's bound
                            through leadSpanFor, and builds the dump text and
                            the netlist from it - 1 + TOOL_MAX_SPAN_HOLES,
                            1 + maxSpanHoles, and minSpanHoles - 1. So a
                            datasheet revision moves the fixture with the module
                            rather than stranding it, and NO SPAN FIGURE EXISTS
                            ANYWHERE IN THE FIXTURE OR THE TEST.
                            THIS CORRECTS A FALSE CLAIM THIS FILE CARRIED. They
                            were static .dump files, which baked the derived row
                            in - `AT 17,1`, `AT 5,1`, `AT 4,1` - while this
                            paragraph asserted no span figure appeared in any
                            fixture. A provenance file that misdescribes its own
                            fixtures is worse than none, because the next reader
                            trusts it. The files are deleted and the claim is
                            now true rather than softened.
                            The constructor also ASSERTS the derived span still
                            offends its constraint, so a revision that moved a
                            bound far enough fails loudly instead of leaving a
                            fixture that quietly tests nothing.
                            span-above-reach names a FILM CAPACITOR and not the
                            resistor, and that is forced: the resistor's own
                            maxSpanHoles IS the tool's ceiling, so no span can
                            separate HC4 from HC5 on it.
                            span-below-minimum names the WIDE FILM CAPACITOR for
                            the mirrored reason, and it named the resistor until
                            2026-10-13. lead-span.ts now derives an axial
                            family's floor from the mounting the owner uses -
                            stood on end, where the body is not between the
                            holes - so the DIN0207's minSpanHoles is the tool's
                            own floor and no span on it separates HC9 from HC4
                            either. The offends guard above CAUGHT that: the
                            derived span fell to 1 hole and the fixture refused
                            by name rather than going quiet.

over-stock                  HAND-WRITTEN. The healthy board with its parts
                            spread so BOUNDS exceeds the stock's 27 columns. The
                            stock is read from stripboard/rules.json, not
                            written here.

over-stock-wire-outside-    HAND-WRITTEN. HC6's SECOND fixture, and the one
bounds                      without which finding 4 is untested: BOUNDS is
                            INSIDE the stock (0,0 6,26, so 27 columns) while a
                            WIRE end lies at column 27, past both. A grader
                            reading BOUNDS alone passes this board. The
                            fabrication extent refuses it and NAMES THE WIRE.

solder-outside-bounds       HAND-WRITTEN, and it is the HOLDS half of a pair. A
                            SOLDER hole lies outside BOUNDS but INSIDE the
                            stock, so HC6 holds AND still reports the
                            discrepancy. Without it, "the detail reports both
                            figures" would be asserted only where the verdict
                            was already a failure, and could not show that the
                            reporting is separate from the verdict.

schematic-delta             HAND-WRITTEN REPORT, over the healthy board: a
                            non-empty `Schematic delta` section, exit 1. The
                            discriminating fact this pins is that a MATCHING
                            board has no such heading AT ALL, so an absent
                            heading and an unreadable report must not both
                            resolve to "no delta".

two-nets-shorted            HAND-WRITTEN, AND IT IS NO LONGER TASK 4'S BOARD.
                            Three 1x02 headers chained across four strips: J1
                            spans strips 0-1, J2 spans 1-2, J3 spans 2-3, and
                            the reference puts J1.2 on `mid` and J2.1 on
                            `other`, so those two nets meet on strip 1. The
                            short is two nets sharing a strip WITHOUT any part
                            straddling one.
                            WHY IT WAS REBUILT. It was Task 4's short - that
                            file's WHOLE board with its CUT line removed -
                            reused so the grader and the equivalence module were
                            held against one artifact. But that board's R2
                            straddles a single strip with BOTH leads on it,
                            which is what makes it a short AND is exactly what
                            HC10's placement half forbids, at a 3-hole span
                            below the resistor's recorded minimum of 5. So HC8's
                            fixture was also failing HC9 and HC10, and a fixture
                            that fails three constraints cannot show which one
                            it is for. The overlap was avoidable, so it was
                            removed; grade.test.ts now asserts this board's
                            failing set is EXACTLY [HC8].
                            The drift guard in equivalence.test.ts is deleted
                            rather than weakened, because its subject is gone:
                            the two boards are now meant to differ, and that
                            file carries the reason where the test was. Nothing
                            is lost - this board is still read through
                            netlistEquivalence, by HC8 itself, in the V4 table.
                            **THE BOARD-LEVEL SHORT FIXTURE IS OB5 AND THIS IS
                            NOT IT.** This is hand-written dump text. The
                            end-to-end claim - that a REAL VeroRoute board
                            carrying a short exits 0 under --check while HC8
                            rejects it - is UNPROVEN and is owner-blocked:
                            22,574 binary invocations produced zero shorts,
                            because --check's completeness is paint-based, so no
                            gesture can both create a short and leave every net
                            complete. Nothing here may be read as evidence for
                            that claim.

round-pin-pattern           HAND-WRITTEN. HC10's FOOTPRINT-half fixture. It
                            names SYNTHETIC:Ring_5Pin_D10mm, a five-pin
                            ring registered only in grade-fixtures.ts's own maps
                            and deliberately NOT in PIN_PATTERNS, because
                            PIN_PATTERNS holds the footprints this repository
                            places and nothing else - and every one of those
                            decomposes into rows, so no recorded footprint
                            exercises admitPattern's across-strip refusal. The
                            ring's classification is DERIVED by classifyPads
                            from its pad coordinates, never asserted, so it is a
                            ring because its geometry is a ring.

rows-along-a-strip          HAND-WRITTEN. HC10's PLACEMENT-half fixture, and it
                            is the INVERSE of what the task brief asked for.
                            The brief wanted a decomposable footprint turned so
                            its rows run ACROSS the strips. The owner settled it
                            the other way on 2026-10-11: *"dips should span
                            strips with a cut down the middle, like a
                            breadboard."* So the fixture that must FAIL puts one
                            of a DIP-16's two eight-pin rows ALONG a single
                            strip, which puts every pin of that row on one piece
                            of copper. No pad coordinate and no row count is
                            written into the test: it reads the rows through the
                            recorded pattern.
                            The brief's wording was measured against the
                            committed boards before being replaced - it refused
                            13 of 16, 27 of 34 and 10 of 12 placed parts on
                            three layouts that pass `make check`. See
                            docs/stripboard/pipeline-verification.md section 3.

rows-across-the-strips      HAND-WRITTEN. The POSITIVE control for the placement
                            half, and the mounting the owner describes: the same
                            DIP-16 with its sixteen pins two to a strip across
                            eight strips, one from each row. Without it the
                            placement half could refuse every multi-row part and
                            every negative fixture would still pass.

PROVENANCE OF THE TWO CAPTURES
------------------------------
  cuts-unresolved.dump
    input board  boards/transistor-preamp-lab/transistor-preamp-lab.perfboard.vrt
    command      veroroute --dump-board <that path>
    binary       .tools/veroroute-perfboard at commit
                 ed6c5a64eb5125346e8b0bc0b434b332c7750bb6, which is what
                 veroroute.pin pins
    sha256       ccd0b28799d5e20591294935d1bedef5ff8fb3978ba6cbb8d5340250418990ff

  cuts-unresolved.report
    command      veroroute --check <that path> --netlist <a fresh export>
    the export   produced by this repository's own lowering path,
                 exportNetlistFor() in tools/perfboard/check.ts, which is the
                 same one `make check` and the write verbs use
    exit         1, recorded in cuts-unresolved.status

  The three span fixtures have no files at all - see their entry above.

  floated-part.dump is HAND-WRITTEN and is NOT a capture - see its entry above.
  The real capture it mirrors is tests/fixtures/pultec-low-boost-c19-floated.dump
  with its own provenance file, unchanged by this directory.

WHAT MAY NOT BE CONCLUDED FROM ANY OF IT
----------------------------------------
These fixtures establish that each constraint CAN fail and fails for its own
reason. They establish nothing about any real board. The evidence that the
grader is pointed at reality is tests/stripboard/grade-checkpoint.test.ts, which
runs all ten over two committed layouts; and the one board there on which all
ten hold is transistor-preamp-feedback, which passes `make check` today.
